title: Less Is More
objective: After this level you can explain Mies van der Rohe's minimalism.
summary: Mies's motto was less is more. In his Barcelona Pavilion, thin steel columns hold the roof so stone and glass walls stand freely; his glass Farnsworth House met a river that ignored the plans.

cards.headline: Mies's Barcelona Pavilion was taken apart in 1930. Then it came back.
cards.body: Ludwig Mies van der Rohe and Lilly Reich designed it as Germany's pavilion for the 1929 Barcelona International Exposition. After the fair, it was dismantled. From 1983 to 1986 it was rebuilt on its original site. Why rebuild a building that was so small and held so little?

cards.headline: Less is more
cards.body: That was Mies's motto: less is more, an architecture of elegant simplicity. (He later ran the Bauhaus, from 1930 until the Nazi regime forced it to close in 1933.) In the pavilion, eight slender chrome-clad steel columns hold up a flat roof. That frees the walls, of glass, travertine, green marble and golden onyx, to stand wherever he wanted, like screens you wander between. Few parts, rich materials, nothing extra: the fewest, finest pieces doing all the talking.

cards.headline: A glass box on a floodplain
cards.body: The Farnsworth House near Chicago, designed in 1945 and built in 1950-51, is less at its purest: a glass box raised on steel on the floodplain of the Fox River. With glass on every side, the outdoors becomes the decoration. Mies set its floor one foot above the highest flood recorded at the time. The river didn't read the plans. In the 1996 flood, water stood more than five feet deep inside.

mascot.line: Less wall, more view. Also, occasionally, more river.

cards.headline: Mies: pared down
learned: Barcelona Pavilion (1929, rebuilt 1983-86): steel columns, free walls
Walls of glass, travertine, marble and onyx
Farnsworth House: a glass box that floods

questions.prompt: Which motto sums up Mies van der Rohe's architecture?

options.label: A house is a machine for living in
Build it like a tree stands
Every wall should carry the roof
options.rationale: Mies freed his walls from carrying.

questions.explanation: Mies's motto, less is more, sums up his architecture of elegant simplicity.

questions.prompt: Mies raised the Farnsworth House above the floodplain. Why did floodwater still get inside?

options.label: He built it right at ground level
options.rationale: It is raised on steel above the ground.

options.label: Its glass walls leaked in heavy rain
options.rationale: The water came from river floods.

options.label: Later floods rose higher than the record he designed for
The river was moved closer after it was built
options.rationale: The floods simply rose higher than expected.

questions.explanation: Mies set the floor one foot above the highest flood then recorded; in 1996, water stood more than five feet deep inside.

questions.prompt: How is the Barcelona Pavilion like Le Corbusier's Dom-ino frame from Level 73?

options.label: Both rest on thick stone walls
Both were designed as factory kits for housing
options.rationale: The pavilion was an exhibition building.

options.label: Both are covered in broken tile
Slender supports carry the roof, so walls go anywhere

questions.explanation: In the pavilion, eight steel columns carry the roof; in the Dom-ino, six posts carry the floors. Either way, the walls are free.
